demo.accountsText: Leave the demo to add your IB account.

welcome.title: Your Interactive Brokers options, read strategy by strategy.
welcome.subtitle: Wheel, LEAPS, Condors: the coverage of each sale, when to buy back, the capital committed and the return — computed in your browser, from your IB statements.

positions.title: Every sale, its coverage
positions.text: Cash, shares, LEAPS or spread: each option sold shows what covers it, and what is not covered flashes in the title bar. A buyback decision accounts for the time left, not only the price.
positions.alt: Positions with their coverage and the buyback decision

wheel.title: The Wheel, cycle by cycle
wheel.text: Puts sold, assignments, covered calls and shares called away follow one another on the underlying's chart, at the price of each lot.

journal.title: Rebuilt journals
journal.text: Each strategy has its journal, its tied-up capital and its monthly return, recomputed from your transaction history.

condors.title: One condor per row
condors.text: Credit received, closing cost, realized and unrealized P/L; the legs unfold under their condor.

more.title: And also
items: A full history, filterable by column
A Consistency page that checks positions and cash
A Sector and Score table shared by your accounts

privacy.title: Your data does not leave your computer
privacy.text: All the computing happens in your browser. The server never sees your transactions or your positions; the backup, optional, is encrypted before it leaves.

steps.title: Import a statement
steps.text: Download an activity statement from your Interactive Brokers client portal and drop it into the app: that is enough to see everything.

steps.title: Automate the update
steps.text: Allow a read-only automatic download, which Interactive Brokers calls a “Flex Query”: your data updates every day, with no new file.

steps.title: Follow the day live, if you wish
steps.text: A small optional program, installed on your computer, reads Interactive Brokers' trading software (TWS) to show your positions and your result for the day.

items.q: Which strategies does the app follow?
items.a: Three option strategies: the Wheel (selling puts, then calls on the shares you receive), LEAPS (long-dated call options) and Iron Condors. Every other trade stays visible, grouped under “Others”.

items.q: What if only one strategy interests me?
items.a: You choose the active strategies of each account, on the Data sources page. A new account starts with the Wheel alone: add LEAPS or Iron Condors only if you trade them. An inactive strategy no longer shows in the menu, and its trades are filed under “Others”.

items.q: Do I have to give my Interactive Brokers username and password?
items.a: Never. You import a statement you downloaded yourself from your Interactive Brokers client portal, or you allow a read-only automatic download, which Interactive Brokers calls a “Flex Query”. The app never places an order.

items.q: Do I need to create an account on this site?
items.a: No. The app works without signing up and your data stays on your computer. An account, by invitation, only adds two options: downloading your statements automatically even without the small optional program installed on your computer, and keeping an encrypted copy of your data to find it on another device.

items.q: Does it work without an internet connection?
items.a: Yes, once it has been opened: it installs like an app and keeps your data on your computer. Only updating your data from Interactive Brokers needs a connection.

app.title: The application
app.text: IB Analyzer analyzes your Interactive Brokers portfolios, stocks and options: coverage of your option sales and required cash, Wheel, LEAPS and Condor journals rebuilt from your history, full history, positions and statistics per strategy. The strategies followed are chosen for each account in Data sources.
app.privacy: Your data stays in this browser: the server never sees your transactions or your positions.
app.sources: The application can draw on several data sources, filtering out duplicates automatically.
tiers: HTML activity statements: a data export provided by Interactive Brokers that you load into the application by hand. They can bring in recent data as well as data older than a year, and they are the quickest way to get a first look at the application.
Flex Queries: an export format provided by Interactive Brokers that automates the import. It gives you data as fresh as yesterday's market close. Flex Queries cannot import data older than 365 days.
The local agent, optional, adds today's positions and fills. It also collects the data the charts need. It cannot fetch any history: it comes on top of the other sources.
app.history: For the application to work well, importing your whole history is strongly recommended. That is what makes it possible to check that every transaction is there and that together they rebuild the last known values of your portfolio.

offline.title: Install the app, work with the server down
items: Install the app from the browser menu: "Install app" in Chrome and Edge, Share → "Add to Home Screen" in Safari on iPhone. It then opens in its own window; in Chrome and Edge it sees the same data as the tab. On iPhone, the app added to the Home Screen has its own storage and starts empty: restore the encrypted backup (Settings) or re-import the statements.

A browser that has opened the site before still opens it while the server is under maintenance: your data lives in this browser. Only the Flex sync relayed by the server and the backup wait for it to come back.
When a new version is published, a banner offers to reload; every tab switches to the new version together.

manual.name: 1. Manual import
manual.summary: The application runs in your browser. You download an activity statement from the Interactive Brokers website and import it by hand. The data stops at the statement's date, yesterday at best, and there are no price charts.

agent.name: 2. Automatic with the local agent
agent.summary: The application runs in your browser and talks to the local agent, a small program installed on your computer. The agent fetches your Flex Queries from Interactive Brokers and reads TWS on your machine: positions close to real time, today's fills, price charts. Nothing goes through the server.

server.name: 3. Automatic through the server
server.summary: The application runs in your browser. Without the local agent, the IB Analyzer server relays your Flex Queries to Interactive Brokers, which takes a server account and being signed in. The data stops at yesterday's close, and there are no price charts. See section 4.

values.transit: the Flex token and response, in transit

statement.title: 1. Get an activity statement
statement.portal: The Client Portal is the Interactive Brokers website where you manage your account and download your statements, the one you sign in to with your IB username. It is not Trader Workstation, the platform where you place your orders.
statement.text: In the Client Portal: Performance & Reports › Statements › Activity. Choose the longest period offered, the HTML format, and download.
items: One statement per year to go back further: "Data sources › Import files" accepts several files at once and writes them in the order of their periods.
The file is kept in this browser so it can be replayed; "Replay the statements" rebuilds everything from the kept files.
A statement also carries your positions and your cash at the end of its period: a single file is enough to fill the app.

flex.title: 2. Set up a Flex Query
flex.text: In the Client Portal: Performance & Reports › Flex Queries. Create an Activity Flex Query, period "Last 365 days", format XML.
flex.selectAll: In each section, tick "Select All" rather than fields one by one: it is faster, and nothing will be missing the day the app reads one more column.
flex.corporateActions: Corporate Actions is the only one whose absence triggers no warning: without it, splits and mergers go missing in silence.
flex.token: Then enable the Flex Web Service and copy the token; note the query's id. Enter both in "Data sources › Flex Query".
flex.relay: Interactive Brokers does not accept a Flex call made directly from a browser: it needs a relay. The local agent (recommended) does it from your machine, without the token ever going through the server — see section 3. Failing that, the server can relay, as a fallback — see section 4. With neither, stay with HTML statements.
flex.missing: What the app cannot find is listed in Data sources at every sync.

what.title: 3. The local agent, optional
what.tws: TWS, short for Trader Workstation, is the Interactive Brokers desktop application, the one where you place your orders. The local agent is a small program you install on your machine: it reads TWS and hands what it reads to the application running in your browser, directly, on your machine. The steps below follow one another in order; allow about ten minutes the first time.
what.text: The agent talks only to the application open in your browser and to Interactive Brokers, never to the server. It stores nothing: positions, cash and today's fills never leave your computer. It also relays the application's Flex Query calls to Interactive Brokers, keeping nothing: in "local agent only" mode, the Flex token never goes through the server. Without it, the app works with statements, and with Flex Query if you let the server relay (section 4).
what.dayValues: Day chg and Daily P&L come from the local agent: a portfolio rebuilt from a statement or a Flex response leaves them at "—", as does a contract bought or sold today.

terminal.title: Before you start: the terminal
terminal.text: Installing takes a few commands typed in a terminal: a window where you write instructions to the computer instead of clicking. No programming needed: copy each grey command on this page with its Copy button, paste it into the terminal and press Enter.
open: macOS: open Spotlight (⌘ + Space), type "Terminal" and press Enter.
Windows: open the Start menu, type "PowerShell" and click Windows PowerShell. No need to run it as administrator.
Linux: Ctrl + Alt + T on most distributions, otherwise look for "Terminal" among your applications.
terminal.paste: To paste: ⌘ + V on macOS, Ctrl + V or a right click on Windows, Ctrl + Shift + V on Linux. One command at a time: paste it, press Enter, then wait for the terminal to hand back control — a new line with a blinking cursor — before the next one. The messages that matter are explained below.

uv.title: A. Install uv
uv.text: uv is a free tool, published by the company Astral, that installs programs written in Python. The agent is written in Python: uv downloads the right Python version for it and everything it needs, in a folder of its own, without changing anything else on your computer. You install it once.
uv.reopen: Once it is installed, close the terminal and open a new one: that is how it finds the uv command. To check, this command must print a version number:
uv.notFound: If the terminal says uv cannot be found ("command not found", "is not recognized"), it almost always means it was not reopened.

install.title: B. Install the agent
install.text: This command downloads the agent from this site and installs it. It ends with "Installed 1 executable: ib-tws-agent".
install.path: If it adds an "is not on your PATH" warning, run the following command, then close and reopen the terminal:
install.update: To update the agent, run the same command again after the site is updated: it installs the version this site serves. If it answers "is already installed", you already have that version. To uninstall the agent:
install.unavailable: This server does not serve the agent package: in development, run pnpm build:agent.

configure.title: C. Configure and start it
configure.origin: For safety, the agent only answers the sites you told it about. This command, run once, gives it this site's address; it answers "Added …".
configure.run: This command starts the agent. It prints nothing and the terminal does not hand back control: that is expected, the agent is running. Leave this window open while you use the site; you may minimize it.
configure.stop: To stop the agent, press Ctrl + C in that window, or close it. Next time, open a terminal and run ib-tws-agent alone: installing and configuring are done.
configure.others: For another site, add its address too, then restart the agent. ib-tws-agent origin list shows the saved addresses, ib-tws-agent origin remove followed by an address drops one.

tws.title: D. Set up the TWS API
tws.text: In TWS: Configuration › API › Settings. TWS must be open and logged in for live data; relaying Flex Query does not need it.
items: Note the "Socket port": one port per account, each TWS has its own. If you run several TWS instances, give them distinct ports, for example 7501 for the first, 7502 for the second, and so on.
"Read-Only API" can stay ticked: the agent never places an order.

chrome.title: E. The browser's permission
chrome.text: The first time, Chrome asks whether this site may reach your local network: that is the agent on your machine. Accept.

port.title: F. Fill in the port
port.text: In Data sources, Local agent section, enter the account's TWS port. It is only needed for live data, not to relay Flex Query. When everything is in place, the section shows "Agent detected" with its version; otherwise, check that the window from step C is still open.

server.title: 4. The server, optional
server.intro: The application does not need the server. A server account, by invitation, opens only two things, both optional: the Flex Query relay when the local agent is missing, and an encrypted backup of your data. It never sees your transactions or your positions.

relay.title: Relaying Flex Query through the server: a fallback mode
relay.text: If you cannot install the local agent, the server can relay your Flex Queries to Interactive Brokers. Sign in to your server account, then choose this relay for the account in "Data sources › Flex Query". The Flex token and the Interactive Brokers response then pass through the server, without being logged or kept there.
relay.degraded: It is a fallback mode: the data stops at yesterday's close, and everything that comes from the agent — today's positions and fills, day P&L and change, price charts — stays missing. As soon as you can, prefer the local agent.

backup.title: Backing up your data, encrypted
backup.text: Entirely optional, the backup lets you find your work again from another machine or another browser: your accounts and their settings, your imported statements, your history, your sector table. On the new browser, sign in, then choose "Settings › Backup › Restore".
backup.encrypted: Your data is encrypted in your browser before it leaves, with a key protected by a passphrase you choose. The server keeps only an unreadable block and never sees the passphrase or the key: no one, not even us, can recover it, and once forgotten, the backup is lost for good.

security.title: 5. Your data's security
security.intro: Your data stays on your computer. Nothing goes to the server unless you turn it on, and whatever goes there is encrypted.

local.title: On your computer: protected by your session
local.text: Your accounts, statements, transactions and positions are stored in your browser, on your computer, and nowhere else. They are protected the same way as a spreadsheet saved on your disk: by your session password. Someone who cannot open your session cannot read them; someone who opens it can see them, as they would see your other files.
advice: Lock your session when you leave your computer, as you would for your other documents.
Avoid a shared computer or a guest session: whoever has access to it would see your data.
The file made by "Settings › Export a file" is plain, unencrypted: keep it as you would keep a bank statement.

server.title: On the server: nothing by default, encrypted if you turn it on
server.text: As long as you turn nothing on, no portfolio data leaves your computer. If you turn on the backup, your data is encrypted in your browser before it leaves, with your passphrase: the server only receives an unreadable block. Neither the host nor the administrator can read it. Choose a long passphrase that you use nowhere else. If you have the server relay your Flex Queries, your Flex token passes through it, without being logged or kept.
server.invitation: Using the server requires an invitation, to keep its traffic limited: no one can sign up freely. Your server account is protected by a password, and you can add two-step verification with an authenticator app (Settings).

agent.title: The local agent: on your computer, read-only
agent.text: The agent only answers requests coming from your own computer and from the sites you gave it. It reads your positions in TWS but places no orders.
